'''Rudolf Zahradník''' (20 October 1928{{spnd}}31 October 2020) was a Czech [[chemist]] in the field of [[quantum chemistry]] and [[molecular spectroscopy]]. He held research positions at the [[Institute of Occupational Medicine]] and went on to serve as the first director of the J Heyrovsky Institute of Physical Chemistry, president of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]] and chairman of the [[Learned Society of the Czech Republic]], after the [[Velvet Revolution]]. During the 1980s, he taught future German leader [[Angela Merkel]], who was then on an internship in [[Czechoslovakia]]. He held a doctorate from the [[University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague]].

==Early life and career ==
Zahradník was born in [[Bratislava]] (then in [[Czechoslovakia]], now in [[Slovakia]]) on 20 October 1928.<ref name=cu/><ref name=jh>{{cite web |title=Professor Rudolf Zahradník October, 20th 1928 till October, 31st 2020 |url=https://www.jh-inst.cas.cz/news/professor-rudolf-zahradnik-october-20th-1928-till-october-31st-2020 |publisher=J. Heyrovsky Institute of Physical Chemistry |accessdate=3 November 2020}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Junák]] scout movement and decided to study chemistry when he read an article on [[invisible ink]] at grammar school.<ref name=roz>{{cite news |title=Zemřel Rudolf Zahradník. Fyzikálnímu chemikovi a mentorovi kancléřky Merkelové bylo 92 let |url=https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/rudolf-zahradnik-akademie-ved-veda-angela-merkelova-kvantova-chemie_2010312019_gak |accessdate=2 November 2020 |work=iROZHLAS |language=cs}}</ref><ref name=prague>{{cite news |title=Pioneering Czech chemist and mentor of Angela Merkel, Rudolf Zahradník, dies aged 92 |url=https://english.radio.cz/pioneering-czech-chemist-and-mentor-angela-merkel-rudolf-zahradnik-dies-aged-92-8698910 |accessdate=3 November 2020 |work=Radio Prague International |date=2 November 2020 |language=en}}</ref> He graduated from the [[University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague]] in 1952, one of his teachers there was [[Jaroslav Koutecký]].<ref name=cu/><ref name=roz/> Four years later he obtained a Ph.D. in [[chemistry]] from the same university.<ref name=cu>{{cite news|url=https://www.clarkson.edu/news/president-czech-republic-academy-sciences-rudolf-zahradnik-awarded-clarkson-university|title=President Of Czech Republic Academy Of Sciences Rudolf Zahradnik Awarded Clarkson University Honorary Degree|date=17 May 1998|accessdate=23 October 2019}}{{Dead link|date=November 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> 
Having previously been considered a bad influence on his students, Zahradník was able to obtain a research position after the [[Khrushchev Thaw]] relaxed Soviet restrictions on Czechoslovakia.<ref name=prague/> He studied the relations between chemical structure and biological activity at the [[Institute of Occupational Medicine]] and theory of chemical reactivity and molecular spectroscopy at the Institute of Physical Chemistry of the Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences<ref name=rcptm>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcptm.com/prof-rudolf-zahradnik/|title=Prof. Rudolf Zahradník|accessdate=23 October 2019}}</ref> before being awarded a [[Doctor of Science]] degree by them in 1967. In 1959, Zahradník joined the faculty of Natural Sciences at [[Charles University]] and in 1961 served as a head of the Applied Quantum Chemistry Group at the Institute of Physical Chemistry, Czechoslovak Academy of Sciences. In the 1980s he taught [[Angela Merkel]] while she was on an internship in [[Czechoslovakia]] several times. They stayed in contact and she also visited him on his ninetieth birthday.<ref name=cu/>

==Career after the Velvet Revolution ==
Between 1990 and 1993 Zahradník served as the first director of the J Heyrovsky Institute of Physical Chemistry before joining [[Clarkson University]].<ref name=cu/> During this period he has been described as "pushing forward the frontiers of [[quantum chemistry]]" and helped to bring young chemists into the field.<ref name=jh/> From 1993 to 2001 he was president of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]] and in 1994 became founding chairman of the [[Learned Society of the Czech Republic]], holding the post until 1997.<ref name=rcptm/><ref name=roz/> He was awarded the Czech Republic's [[Medal of Merit (Czech Republic)|Medal of Merit]] in 1998 and the [[Austrian Decoration for Science and Art]] in 1999.<ref name=roz/>

Zahradník was a recipient of a doctorate ''honoris causa'' from the [[TU Dresden]] and [[University of Fribourg]] (both in 1993), and from the [[University of Pardubice]] and [[Georgetown University]] in 1994 and 1996 respectively. He was also honored with doctorate ''honoris causa'' degrees from [[Charles University|Charles]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cuni.cz/UKEN-139.html|title=Honorary Doctorates|publisher=Charles University|accessdate=23 October 2019}}</ref> and [[Clarkson University|Clarkson universities]] in 1998.<ref name=iqms>{{cite web|url=http://www.iaqms.org/members/zahradnik.php|title=Rudolf Zahradník|publisher=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science|accessdate=23 October 2019|archive-date=7 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171207172714/http://www.iaqms.org/members/zahradnik.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He published more than 350 papers and 10 books especially on [[quantum chemistry]] problems.<ref name=iqms/> He died on 31 October 2020.<ref name=roz/>
